guide.title: Setup guide
guide.description: Steps to install the agent on a monitored host.

auditd.title: Make sure auditd is enabled and running
auditd.body: The agent monitors through the auditd audit log. Run the following commands on the monitored host.
auditd.fix: If it is disabled or stopped, enable and start it with:

actions.title: Check the actions in auditd.conf
actions.body: Check what auditd does when the disk runs low or fails.
actions.warning: If space_left_action, admin_space_left_action, disk_full_action or disk_error_action is HALT or SINGLE, disk conditions can halt the host or drop it into single-user mode. Change them so monitoring never stops your services.
actions.change: Edit /etc/audit/auditd.conf and use SYSLOG, SUSPEND or ROTATE, for example:
actions.restartNote: Many distributions do not allow restarting auditd with systemctl restart, so use the service command.

rotate.title: Check log rotation
rotate.body: Make sure the audit log is rotated so it does not fill the disk.
rotate.expect: Check that max_log_file_action is ROTATE and num_logs is 2 or more (for example 5). Set them like this if needed:
rotate.restart: If you changed anything, restart auditd with sudo service auditd restart as in the previous step.

token.title: Issue a token
token.body: An administrator issues one token per host.
token.note: The token value is shown only when issued. It is bound to the machine ID of the first host that connects and cannot be used on other hosts.

init.title: Initialize and start the agent
init.body: Place mimamori on the monitored host and initialize it with the issued token. Replace <token> with the issued value.
init.stdin: The token is read from standard input, so it is not passed as an argument and does not appear in the process list.
init.fingerprint: Passing the fingerprint above with --ca-fingerprint verifies the central server on the very first connection.
init.overwrite: Add --overwrite to re-initialize a host that is already initialized.
init.start: When initialization finishes, start the agent:
init.otherUrls: Any of the agent server URLs listed above can be used.

auto.title: What the agent handles automatically
auto.body: The agent configures the auditd settings it needs by itself.
auto.globals: It overrides global settings (backlog_wait_time 0, failure 1) through its own rules file without editing the OS defaults:
auto.osDefaults: The OS default configuration files (audit.rules and auditd.conf) are left untouched.
auto.never: It removes the default rule that suppresses auditing (-a never,task), which some distributions such as Amazon Linux 2023 ship by default. Check for it with:
auto.restartTitle: Processes started before the removal are not audited
auto.restartBody: Processes started before -a never,task was removed are not audited until they restart. Restart services such as the web server and php-fpm after installation. The agent details page lists processes that are not audited.

reinit.title: Re-initializing
reinit.body: Re-initialize with a new token value and --overwrite when:
reinit.caseExpired: The token expired (the agent could not connect before expiry, so it was not renewed)
reinit.caseCa: The agent missed a private CA rotation (for example because it was stopped) and can no longer connect
reinit.after: After re-initializing, start the agent again:

central.title: About the central host
central.body: The central server includes a built-in agent that monitors its own host. Perform steps 1 to 3 on the central host as well so auditd is enabled and running. Without auditd the built-in agent stops and a warning appears at the top of every page.
